exercises.label: 4. Make a 3-digit number ending with 5.
exercises.answer_key: Open-ended (multiple valid answers). The 5 is fixed in the ones place; the other two boxes must be filled with two DIFFERENT digits drawn from the remaining bag digits {2, 7, 9} (each digit token appears once in the bag). Any valid arrangement works, e.g. 275, 295, 725, 925, 795, or 975 (using two of 2/7/9 in the tens & hundreds places).
exercises.answer_confidence: high (task structure); no single fixed numeric answer

exercises.label: 5. Arrange smallest to largest
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Now, let's arrange these numbers from smallest to the largest: 123, 342, 258, 240, 446.

exercises.instruction_verbatim: Circle the numbers that are greater than 705.
exercises.answer_key: Circle 834, 711, 812 (698 and 590 are both less than 705, so not circled).

exercises.label: Skill Sharpener 2b. Circle numbers less than 512
exercises.instruction_verbatim: Circle the numbers that are less than 512.
exercises.answer_key: Circle 268, 507, 378 (600 and 564 are both greater than 512, so not circled).
